name: Bromo-DragonFLY
toxicities: Several deaths and many hospitalisations, extreme vasoconstriction that can cause severe tissue damage or amputation, and overdose risk from incorrect measurement or mislabelling. Toxicity and long-term effects are unstudied and exact toxic dose unknown. Overdose risk may be higher by non-oral routes and reports severe agitation, confusion, seizures, prolonged hypertension and vasoconstriction; some treatment details carry source-request tags.
effectsSummary: Bromo-DragonFLY is extremely potent with an exceptionally long, unpredictable duration. It is associated with unusually many hospitalisations and deaths; reports describe severe vasoconstriction and tissue damage. The source urges the strictest harm reduction and a trip sitter.
dosageRemark: The archived oral table lists threshold 75 µg, light 100-300 µg, moderate 300-500 µg, strong 500-750 µg, heavy 750 µg+; total duration 1-4 days, onset 2-7 h, comeup 3-6 h, peak 6-12 h, offset 3-8 h, afterglow 12-36 h. User/resource educational compilation, not a recommendation. Because the source reports deaths after mislabelling and an extremely narrow margin, preserve the data only as attributed source information; never treat it as safe-use guidance.
generalRisks: Two deaths in 2011 after people took Bromo-DragonFLY believing it was 2C-E, with others hospitalised. The compound can cause extreme, prolonged vasoconstriction and tissue damage and may be easily overdosed because of high potency and mislabelling. The page itself advises against trying it without the strictest harm reduction, oral-only use and a trip sitter.
longtermRisks: Toxicity and long-term health effects have not been studied; severe vasoconstriction may cause lasting tissue injury or amputation.
saferUse: Not attempting to use the substance without strict harm reduction, a trip sitter and taking it by mouth only are recommended, and volumetric dosing is specifically mentioned.

It reports deaths and many hospitalisations, including cases caused by mislabelling, and says overdose requires emergency medical services. Treatment suggestions on the source page are partly tagged as needing citations.
summary: Bromo-DragonFLY is a very potent, very long-acting psychedelic phenethylamine and benzofuran. It was briefly sold as 2C-B-FLY in 2005 and 2006 and has led to multiple deaths. FreeODwiki warns of severe vasoconstriction and overdose risk, and it is associated with numerous hospitalisations and deaths, including fatal mislabelling cases.
